cards.back: A departure from what is normal or expected. "The warm December day was an aberration in an otherwise frigid winter."
The ability to make good judgments and quick decisions. "Her business acumen led the startup to profitability within a year."
Having mixed or contradictory feelings about something. "He felt ambivalent about moving — excited but also sad to leave."
Something that belongs to a different time period. "The knight wearing a wristwatch was an obvious anachronism in the film."
Suggesting a positive and successful future. "The clear skies on launch day were an auspicious sign for the mission."
Well-meaning and kindly. "The benevolent donor funded scholarships for hundreds of students."
Given to sudden, unpredictable changes of mood or behavior. "The capricious weather shifted from sunshine to hail within minutes."
Clear, logical, and convincing. "She made a cogent argument that persuaded even the skeptics."
A confusing and difficult problem or question. "The budget deficit presented a conundrum with no easy solution."
To make someone weak or infirm. "The illness debilitated him for months before he regained his strength."
To describe or outline with precision. "The report delineated the steps needed to address the crisis."
Intended to teach or instruct. "The novel had a didactic tone, clearly aiming to impart moral lessons."
Essentially different in kind; not able to be compared. "The committee had to reconcile disparate viewpoints on the issue."
Fluent and persuasive in speaking or writing. "The eloquent speech moved the audience to a standing ovation."
Based on observation or experience rather than theory. "The study provided empirical evidence supporting the hypothesis."
Difficult to interpret or understand; mysterious. "The Mona Lisa's enigmatic smile has fascinated viewers for centuries."
Lasting for a very short time. "The beauty of cherry blossoms is ephemeral — they bloom for only two weeks."
Open to more than one interpretation; ambiguous. "The politician gave an equivocal answer that satisfied no one."
To make a problem or situation worse. "The drought was exacerbated by record-high temperatures."
Very attentive to detail; meticulous. "The fastidious editor caught every misplaced comma in the manuscript."
Happening by lucky chance. "Their fortuitous meeting at the airport led to a lifelong friendship."
Fond of company; sociable. "The gregarious host made sure every guest felt welcome at the party."
Overused and unoriginal. "The movie relied on hackneyed plot twists that audiences saw coming."
Peculiar to the individual. "Her idiosyncratic habit of humming while working amused her colleagues."
Unable to be affected; not allowing passage through. "He seemed impervious to criticism, continuing his work undeterred."
Intelligently analytical and clear-thinking. "The journalist's incisive questions revealed the flaws in the proposal."
Not harmful or offensive. "What seemed like an innocuous comment turned out to deeply hurt her feelings."
To place side by side for comparison or contrast. "The exhibit juxtaposed ancient artifacts with modern art."
Affected by a lack of energy or enthusiasm. "After the heavy meal, everyone felt lethargic and sluggish."
Expressed clearly; easy to understand. Also: mentally clear. "Despite her fever, she gave a lucid account of the incident."
Showing great attention to detail; very careful. "The meticulous researcher double-checked every data point."
To make less severe or serious. "Sandbags were placed along the river to mitigate flood damage."
Feeling or appearing casually calm and relaxed. "She gave a nonchalant shrug, as if the news didn't bother her."
To make unclear or difficult to understand. "The jargon-filled report seemed designed to obfuscate rather than inform."
A seemingly contradictory statement that reveals a truth. "It's a paradox that standing is more tiring than walking."
Excessively concerned with minor details or rules. "His pedantic corrections of everyone's grammar made him unpopular."
Done without care or interest; mechanical. "The security guard gave a perfunctory glance at the ID and waved us through."
Dealing with things in a practical rather than idealistic way. "She took a pragmatic approach, focusing on what could actually be done."
Not securely held; dangerously likely to fall or collapse. "The hikers found themselves in a precarious position on the narrow ledge."
Producing much fruit, foliage, or many offspring; highly productive. "The prolific author published three novels in a single year."
Complaining in a whining manner. "The querulous passenger complained about everything from the seat to the food."
Stubbornly uncooperative. "The recalcitrant student refused to follow any of the classroom rules."
Having keen mental discernment and good judgment. "The sagacious investor foresaw the market crash and sold early."
Optimistic or positive, especially in a difficult situation. "Despite the setback, she remained sanguine about the project's success."
Unnecessary; more than enough. "The report was full of superfluous details that obscured the main findings."
Reserved or uncommunicative in speech. "The taciturn farmer said little but observed everything."
Very weak or slight; insubstantial. "The connection between the two events seemed tenuous at best."
Present everywhere. "Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern life."
To clear of blame or suspicion. "The new evidence vindicated the defendant after years of wrongful imprisonment."
Having great energy or enthusiasm for a cause. "The zealous volunteers worked through the night to finish the project."
